title: How to Repair a Kitchen Sink Drain Trap — This Old House (analysis)

locations.name: Georgia, USA
locations.basis: Transcript explicitly mentions 'Georgia' as the location where help arrived; country inferred as USA

summary: This This Old House tutorial examines diagnosing and correcting a kitchen sink drainage arrangement that used three traps feeding two basins and a dishwasher. The host plans a single-trap configuration, caps unused branches, and adds a cleanout for future maintenance. The video then reinstalls the garbage disposal to define pipe lengths, taps the dishwasher into the disposal using the built-in knockout, and fabricates a new waste line with PVC fittings and clamps. Finally, the assembly is leak-tested to confirm proper drainage flow and seal integrity.

sections.title: Explain trap function and the current multi-trap setup
sections.description: The presenter describes how a kitchen sink trap creates a water seal to block sewer gases and notes an unusual rough-in that leaves three traps feeding the area.

sections.title: Plan to consolidate into a single trap; cap unused branch; install cleanout
sections.description: The plan is to remove redundant piping, combine to one trap, cap one branch, and install a cleanout to facilitate future maintenance while prepping fittings for cement.

sections.title: Reinstall disposer to establish layout and dishwasher connection
sections.description: The disposer is reinstalled to locate where the drain comes down and to address the dishwasher connection via the knock-out access.

sections.title: Install new T-fitting to provide a branch to the other sink
sections.description: A T-fitting is added to create a branch toward the other sink; the pipe is marked and cut to fit within the allotted window for proper alignment.

sections.title: Measure and cut waist arm and vertical pieces with proper pitch
sections.description: Measurements are taken and components are cut to create the horizontal waist arm and the vertical drop with a slight pitch toward the trap.

sections.title: Connect dishwasher discharge to disposer and secure
sections.description: The dishwasher discharge hose is connected to the disposer, and a stainless steel clamp is used to secure the connection.

sections.title: leak test and final check
sections.description: All joints are checked for leaks; water flows through the newly configured drain, confirming proper function and seal.

featured_techniques.technique: Consolidating multiple kitchen sink traps into a single trap
Installing a cleanout and capping unused branches for future maintenance
Reinstalling and aligning the garbage disposal to determine pipe lengths
Using a disposer knockout plate for the dishwasher connection
Adding a T-fitting to link a second sink
Measuring, marking, and cutting PVC for precise fit
Applying PVC primer and cement to fittings and pipe
Testing for leaks after assembly with water
Securing dishwasher discharge hose with a stainless steel clamp
